subject: Linguistics
title: Sense and Reference
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Sense and Reference.

hook.text: 'The morning star' and 'the evening star' both refer to Venus—but they mean different things.

buildup.text: Reference is what a word points to in the world; sense is the concept it evokes.

discovery.text: Frege introduced this distinction in 1892—it's still foundational in semantics.

twist.text: Fictional names like 'Sherlock Holmes' have sense but no real-world reference at all.

climax.text: Sense and reference are both part of meaning—but they operate on different planes.

punchline.text: Same target, different lens—that's the sense/reference split.
